2211.text: In Lev.16.21 'confess' renders the Hithpael sense (confession of sin transferred onto the scapegoat), a distinct nuance from the Hiphil 'give thanks/praise' sense seen elsewhere in this batch (e.g. Ps.7.17, Ps.18.49) -- here the impact is ritual/transferential rather than doxological, marking the negative/penitential pole of the same root.

2215.text: No other M-code characteristic co-occurs with H3034 in Lev.16.21; the confession act stands alone amid role-only tags (M-codes present belong to non-home strongs but none are flagged as sharing this cluster's relational chain in prior context, and no prior pass exists for this verse).

3215.text: Yes, the mechanism differs across contexts: in the cultic/temple context it operates through appointed liturgical office and musical instrumentation (1Chr.16.4, 2Chr.5.13, 1Chr.25.3 -- Levites appointed, with lyre/trumpets); in the personal-devotional context it operates through spontaneous individual speech-vow (Ps.9.1, Ps.86.12 'with my whole heart'); in the penitential context it operates through a required ritual or intercessory-prayer act (Lev.16.21's scapegoat confession, Dan.9.4's extended prayer of confession) -- three distinct mechanisms (institutional/musical, personal/vocal, ritual/legal) all realizing the same root verb.

11893.text: It is given by God, in the heart: "I will give them one heart and one way, that they may fear me forever"; "I will put the fear of me in their hearts, that they may not turn from me"; "Oh that they had such a heart as this always, to fear me"; prayed for: "unite my heart to fear your name"; on the shoot of Jesse rests "the Spirit of knowledge and the fear of the Lord. And his delight shall be in the fear of the Lord"

11900.text: It governs conduct toward the weak and toward others.

12431.text: Thoughts are fully open to God and to Jesus.

12447.text: Inner reasoning becomes outward quarrel when it is shared and set on one's own standing

12574.text: Face D, fearing God as a way of life: fear, fears, feared, fearing, reverence, God-fearing and worship; not a passing state but a standing, commanded, learned, taught, given, lived, joined with walking, serving, keeping and turning from evil.

12589.text: Heart near or far: fear taught by men while "their hearts are far from me" set against fear put "in their hearts" (Isa 29:13; Jer 32:40).

12597.text: As a standing toward God: commanded, learned, given: "what does the Lord your God require of you, but to fear the Lord your God"; "that they may hear and learn to fear the Lord your God"; "I will put the fear of me in their hearts, that they may not turn from me"

12640.text: Where the heart is: Fear "taught by men" while "their hearts are far from me"; fear put "in their hearts"

12673.text: Fear and Inner seat (M47): Fear is felt in the heart; given in the heart; a trembling heart in the curse; the heart firm and not afraid (verses shared or near: 97 / 50).

13182.text: Anger and Inner seat (M47), side by side with fear: fear side, fear felt in the heart; given in the heart; the heart firm and not afraid (1Sa 28:5; Jer 32:40; Psa 112:7); anger side, anger answers a heart turned; burns within; the heat of the spirit; a hard heart stores up wrath (1Ki 11:9; Est 1:12; Eze 3:14; Rom 2:5).

13198.text: What turns or ends God's anger: humbled → wrath turned (2Ch 12:12); Moses prayed → the Lord listened (Deu 9:19); stood in the breach → wrath turned (Psa 106:23); atonement → stood between → plague stopped (Num 16:46–48); jealous with my jealousy → wrath turned back (Num 25:11); wrath satisfied → calm, no more angry (Eze 16:42); with the last plagues → the wrath is finished (Rev 15:1).

13504.text: Face 4E. Asked: heard, or not heard; atonement made: Hits / verses: 4 / 4; Toward: the people; Moses himself; Jerusalem; Other parties named: Moses pleads; Aaron runs with the censer; the angel of the Lord asks; Example verses: Deu 9:19; Deu 3:26; Num 16:46; Zec 1:12.

13561.text: wrath gone out → plague begun → atonement → stood between → plague stopped (Num 16:46–48).

13687.text: Samson: the Spirit's rushing goes with the striking at Ashkelon, and the "hot anger" comes at the end, with its ground given: his wife wept "You only hate me; you do not love me" (Judg 14:16), he told her "because she pressed him hard" (14:17), and his own word is "If you had not plowed with my heifer, you would not have found out my riddle" (14:18); then "Samson's wife was given to his companion" (14:20).

13701.text: "Weeping and gnashing of teeth" stands seven times in the judgment sayings (Mat 8:12; 13:42; 13:50; 22:13; 24:51; 25:30; Luk 13:28); Luke gives the moment: "when you see Abraham and Isaac and Jacob and all the prophets in the kingdom of God but you yourselves cast out" (13:28).

13714.text: Luk 15:28: the elder brother "was angry and refused to go in"; his father came out and entreated him; the complaint that follows (15:29-30) exposes a hidden grievance, "these many years I have served you": the inner state was held behind service, and anger releases it (hidden-behind-act).

14011.text: A burden shared: Moses (H v1 §3.3, "Moses' burden, then the Spirit shared", Num 11:10–17).

14016.text: Betrayal (Judg 14:16–18: the riddle given away through his wife).

14248.text: What it leads to: Withdrawal from what God struck: David will not take the ark home (2Sa 6:10). The anger ends in avoidance, and the ark's blessing goes to Obed-edom instead (6:11); A burden shared: Moses; Obedience with grief: Samuel goes to meet Saul the next morning (15:12).

14258.text: Where it comes from: Hearing (1Sa 11:5–6: "they told him the news of the men of Jabesh"); Betrayal (Judg 14:16–18: the riddle given away through his wife); Seeing: an Israelite brought a Midianite woman "in the sight of Moses and … the whole congregation … while they were weeping" (Num 25:6). "When Phinehas … saw it, he rose … and took a spear" (25:7), and killed them both (25:8); Victory in battle (2Ch 28:6–8).

14538.text: What it does: Atonement carried into the plague: "Take your censer … carry it quickly to the congregation and make atonement for them, for wrath has gone out from the Lord" (Num 16:46). Aaron "ran into the midst … And he stood between the dead and the living, and the plague was stopped" (16:47–48). The priest's body stands on the line; Execution of the leaders: "hang them in the sun before the Lord, that the fierce anger of the Lord may turn away from Israel" (Num 25:4). Then Phinehas's spear (25:7), read in U1 §15 (SP, 25:11); Nothing of the devoted thing kept: "None of the devoted things shall stick to your hand, that the Lord may turn from the fierceness of his anger and show you mercy and have compassion on you" (Deu 13:17).

14610.text: How it co-exists: Isolation. "He has put my brothers far from me … My relatives have failed me, my close friends have forgotten me" (19:13–14). "Men have gaped at me with their mouth" (16:10); Not being able to see God. "Behold, he passes by me, and I see him not" (9:11). "If I summoned him and he answered me, I would not believe that he was listening to my voice" (9:16); A wish not to have been born. "Why did you bring me out from the womb?" (10:18). "leave me alone, that I may find a little cheer" (10:20); Hope beyond the anger, in the same breath. "Oh that you would hide me in Sheol, that you would conceal me until your wrath be past, that you would appoint me a set time, and remember me! … You would call, and I would answer you; you would long for the work of your hands" (14:13, 15). Job asks for a hiding place from God's anger in God's own keeping, and expects God to long for him afterwards.

15026.text: his heart is broken, he looks for pity and comfort and finds none (69:20), and he is given poison and sour wine (69:21; John 19:28–30 is in 10.6).

15224.text: Mocked as king: "kneeling before him, they mocked him, saying, 'Hail, King of the Jews!'" (Mat 27:29); Herod "treated him with contempt and mocked him. Then, arraying him in splendid clothing" (Luk 23:11). Before this, "he made no answer" (23:9); "when they had mocked him, they stripped him of the robe ... and led him away to crucify him" (Mat 27:31; Mar 15:20).

15322.text: He is mocked on that very standing, as king, as prophet and as saviour (Mat 27:29; Luk 22:64; Mar 15:31). He "made no answer" (Luk 23:9), and he prays "Father, forgive them" (Luk 23:34).

15539.text: The anointing at Bethany: Mar 14:3–9; Mat 26:6–13; Joh 12:1–8: The objection: the ointment "could have been sold … and given to the poor" (Mar 14:5; Mat 26:9; Joh 12:5); Who raises it, and how:; Mark: "some … said to themselves indignantly", and "they scolded her" (14:4–5); Matthew: "the disciples … were indignant" (26:8); John: Judas, and John gives the motive: "He said this, not because he cared about the poor, but because he was a thief, and having charge of the moneybag he used to help himself to what was put into it" (12:6); Jesus' answer: "you always have the poor with you, and whenever you want, you can do good for them. But you will not always have me" (Mar 14:7; Mat 26:11; Joh 12:8).

15542.text: Mar 12:42; Luk 21:3: "a poor widow came and put in two small copper coins". Jesus says she "has put in more than all those who are contributing … For they all contributed out of their abundance, but she out of her poverty has put in everything she had, all she had to live on" (Mar 12:43–44; Luk 21:3–4): The measure is what is left, not what is given: "out of their abundance" against "out of her poverty … all she had to live on"; In Mark the scene follows directly on the scribes "who devour widows' houses and for a pretense make long prayers" (12:40). The poor widow gives everything at the treasury, while those who devour widows pray at length for show; I read: the verses name no inner word for her. What they give is the measure Jesus sets; Mar 12:38–44 are cited in 10.5 (the long prayers and the widow; M18 group G). The M09 verse 12:42 and the Luke parallel are not.

15557.text: B: What the verses say: "The poor" spoken of by others to judge an act of devotion, and a motive hidden behind the words.; Verses: Mar 14:5, Mat 26:9, Mat 26:11, Joh 12:5, Joh 12:6, Joh 12:8 (6; one event in three Gospels).

15558.text: C: What the verses say: Giving out of poverty, measured by what is left, not by the amount.; Verses: Mar 12:42, Luk 21:3 (2; one event in two Gospels).

15592.text: What the sight moves in a person, as the verses name it (G-person): "Was not my soul grieved for the needy?" (Job 30:25); "He has pity on the weak and the needy" (Psa 72:13, the king); "you shall not harden your heart or shut your hand" (Deu 15:7); "an unworthy thought in your heart" (Deu 15:9); "Whoever mocks the poor … he who is glad at calamity" (Pro 17:5); "The poor is disliked even by his neighbor" (Pro 14:20); "All a poor man's brothers hate him" (Pro 19:7); "the poor man's wisdom is despised" (Ecc 9:16); "These are only the poor; they have no sense" (Jer 5:4); "no one remembered that poor man" (Ecc 9:15); "the very thing I was eager to do" (Gal 2:10); "pleased to make some contribution for the poor" (Rom 15:26); "not because he cared about the poor" (Joh 12:6); "the master of the house became angry and said … bring in the poor" (Luk 14:21).

15605.text: Verses with no other M-code (27). Unlike the M64 choose verses that were parked (OT-93), these include verses central to the cluster: Num 12:3 (Moses very meek); Mat 23:12, Luk 14:11 and Jam 4:10 (humble yourself and be exalted); Luk 1:52 ("exalted those of humble estate"); 2Sa 6:22 (David "abased in my own eyes"); the widow's offering (Mar 12:42; Luk 21:3).

15839.text: Reverent fear (of God) placed in or governing the heart: "I will put the fear of me in their hearts" (Jer 32:40); "I will give them one heart … that they may fear me forever" (Jer 32:39); "unite my heart to fear your name" (Psa 86:11); "Oh that they had such a heart as this always, to fear me" (Deu 5:29); "my heart stands in awe of your words" (Psa 119:161); Opposite: "harden our heart, so that we fear you not" (Isa 63:17); "Blessed is the one who fears the Lord always, but whoever hardens his heart will fall" (Pro 28:14); "Transgression speaks to the wicked deep in his heart; there is no fear of God before his eyes" (Psa 36:1); [Claude reading] Hardening of heart is set against the fear of God. The fear of God is something God can put into the heart.

15969.text: 2.4 Wisdom entering and staying: "wisdom will come into your heart" (Pro 2:10); "Wisdom rests in the heart of a man of understanding" (Pro 14:33); Revisit 2026-09-28: *nûaḥ* "rest" has three residents: wisdom in the heart of the understanding (Pro 14:33), anger in the heart of fools (Ecc 7:9), the Spirit upon the prophet (Num 11:25; Isa 11:2). See Batch F §9.5.; "teach us to number our days that we may get a heart of wisdom" (Psa 90:12); "I searched with my heart how to cheer my body with wine — my heart still guiding me with wisdom" (Ecc 2:3) — the heart guiding the body's experiment

15970.text: Transmitted: "full of the spirit of wisdom, for Moses had laid his hands on him" (Deu 34:9) [X].; Revisit 2026-09-28: read with Num 27:18 ("a man in whom is the Spirit, and lay your hand on him") and the sequel "So the people of Israel obeyed him". The spirit is present before the hands are laid on, and it is confirmed by others' response. See Batch G §13.1, and compare 2Ki 2:15 and Num 11:25–29 (Batch F §9.5).

16001.text: Keeping: "I kept the matter in my heart" (Dan 7:28); "he who is trustworthy in spirit keeps a thing covered" (Pro 11:13) [H]; "Whoever restrains his words … a cool spirit" (Pro 17:27) [H]; "I told no one what my God had put into my heart" (Neh 2:12)

16021.text: God's Spirit as the true source: "the Spirit of God rushed upon him, and he prophesied" (1Sa 10:10; 19:20, 23); "as soon as the Spirit rested on them, they prophesied" (Num 11:25–26); "that the Lord would put his Spirit on them!" (Num 11:29); Revisit 2026-09-28 (context Num 11:24–29, Batch F §9.5): they prophesied "but they did not continue" (25). Joshua: "stop them" (28). Moses: "Are you jealous for my sake?" (29). The resting Spirit is resisted and then defended, and it is recognised by others.; "I will pour out my Spirit on all flesh; your sons and your daughters shall prophesy" (Joe 2:28; Act 2:17–18); "carried along by the Holy Spirit" — "not by the will of man" (2Pe 1:21)

16116.text: 8.3 Faintness sent into hearts: "I will send faintness into their hearts in the lands of their enemies. The sound of a driven leaf shall put them to flight … they shall fall when none pursues" (Lev 26:36); "panic … fever that consume the eyes and make the heart ache" (Lev 26:16)

16117.text: Revisit: Lev 26:36 extends the Lev 26 reciprocity sequence of Batch F §4. The heart-effects of the curse run from 26:16 to 26:36.

16225.text: Batch F v1 | §1.1, §3, §4, §7, §15 | 1Sa 17:55 as the threshold of 18:1 (G §4); despairing life-hatred (G §6); Lev 26:36 (G §8.3); Judg 19:5, 8, Uriah, Hannah / Nehemiah, Gen 27:25, the Samson sequence (G §3.1, §4, §8.2, §13.3, §3.6); a fifth self-address setting (Judg 5:21) | Batch F v2

16263.text: 1.6 The Spirit speaks through the person: "The Spirit of the Lord speaks by me; his word is on my tongue" (2Sa 23:2) [D1]; "as he spoke to me, the Spirit entered into me and set me on my feet, and I heard him speaking to me" (Eze 2:2; 3:24) [D3]; "How did the Spirit of the Lord go from me to speak to you?" (1Ki 22:24; 2Ch 18:23) [D1]; "the Lord … took some of the Spirit that was on him and put it on the seventy elders … they prophesied" (Num 11:17, 25) [D2]; "David, in the Spirit, calls him Lord" (Mat 22:43) [D2]

16273.text: Heart: "return to me with all your heart" (Joe 2:12); "I will write it on their hearts" (Jer 31:33); "not … with her whole heart, but in pretense" (Jer 3:10); "he who is stout of heart … shall flee away naked" (Amo 2:16); "courage [*heart*] shall fail both king and officials" (Jer 4:9)

16635.text: Speaking, testifying, teaching: Act 1:16; 4:25; 13:2; 20:23; 21:11; 28:25; Heb 3:7; 9:8; 10:15; Mar 12:36; 13:11 ("it is not you who speak, but the Holy Spirit"); Luk 12:12; Joh 14:26 ("bring to your remembrance"); 2Pe 1:21

16794.text: 3.2 The servant's inner sentence: "if that servant says to himself [*in his heart*], 'My master is delayed,' and begins to beat the … servants, and to eat and drink and get drunk" (Luk 12:45; Mat 24:48–49). Context read: Luk 12:42–46; Mat 24:49–51.; The faithful manager feeds the household "at the proper time" (Luk 12:42).; The unfaithful servant says in his heart that the master is delayed → beats → eats and drinks with drunkards → the master "will come on a day when he does not expect him" (46).; → Batch D §10 (inner speech). New here: the inner sentence is followed at once by eating and drinking, then the sudden arrival (§7.6).

16796.text: Moses' burden, then the Spirit shared. Context read: Num 11:10–17.; "why … you lay the burden of all this people on me?" (11); "Did I conceive all this people? … Carry them in your bosom" (12); "kill me at once … that I may not see my wretchedness" (15); "I will take some of the Spirit that is on you and put it on them, and they shall bear the burden … with you" (17) [D2]; [Claude reading] Despair under a burden (like Batch G §6) is answered by distributing the Spirit, not by removing the burden.

16846.text: 6.5 ◆ Fringe (M26): "my beloved with whom my soul is well pleased. I will put my Spirit upon him, and he will proclaim justice" (Mat 12:18) [D1] — God's soul, God's Spirit and justice in one sentence; "the souls of those who had been beheaded … authority to judge was committed" (Rev 20:4); "God appointed a scorching east wind … he asked that he might die" (Jon 4:8) → Batch G §6

16888.text: Lev 26:36 (filed under the people's hearts): "I will send faintness into their hearts … the sound of a driven leaf shall put them to flight" *(Revisit, Batch G §8.3)*

16966.text: The Spirit on people: "as soon as the Spirit rested on them, they prophesied. But they did not continue doing it" (Num 11:25); "the Spirit rested on them … and so they prophesied in the camp" (Num 11:26); "The Spirit of the Lord shall rest upon him, the Spirit of wisdom and understanding" (Isa 11:2); "the Spirit of glory and of God rests upon you" (1Pe 4:14); "The spirit of Elijah rests on Elisha" (2Ki 2:15)

16967.text: Context Num 11:24–29 — the resting Spirit resisted and defended: The Spirit taken from Moses rests on the seventy; they prophesy "but they did not continue" (25).; Eldad and Medad prophesy in the camp (26). Joshua: "My lord Moses, stop them" (28).; Moses: "Are you jealous for my sake? Would that all the Lord's people were prophets, that the Lord would put his Spirit on them!" (29).

17031.text: Jealousy for the Spirit's spread: "Are you jealous for my sake? Would that … the Lord would put his Spirit on them!" (Num 11:29) [D1].

17315.text: OT-95, jealousy (8 verses). Elijah's zeal (1Ki 19:10, 14), God's jealousy (Eze 36:5), heart envy (Pro 23:17; Jam 3:14), Jam 4:5, Num 11:29 and Eze 8:3. Jealousy has faces that differ by whose it is (God's, a husband's, envy of sinners). It needs one account, from the jealousy words, rather than pieces now.

17700.text: W4 The will that would not | Mat 22:3 (with 22:5); Mat 18:30 (with 18:29, 32); Luk 19:14; Joh 7:1 (with 7:3); 1Co 16:12 | The will refusing what is put before it: an invitation, a plea for patience, a reign, a threat, a friend's urging. This extends the existing list in 10.7. | 10.7 *Willing*, *The will meets something put before it*

17776.text: Joh 19:28–30; Psa 69:20–21 | "knowing that all was now finished … 'I thirst'"; sour wine; "It is finished". The psalm sets the thirst beside "I looked for pity, but there was none" | The one who offered water thirsts, and says it knowingly. I read the want spoken, not hidden

17829.text: Luk 15:19–22 | "still a long way off", the father saw, felt compassion, ran; the rehearsed "hired servants" is never said | 10.10 | I read the son's self-rating set aside, not argued with

18067.text: Mark 14:4–7: the poor as a pretext, and doing good "whenever you want".: > "There were some who said to themselves indignantly, 'Why was the ointment wasted like that? For; > this ointment could have been sold for more than three hundred denarii and given to the poor.' And; > they scolded her. But Jesus said, 'Leave her alone … For you always have the poor with you, and; > whenever you want, you can do good for them. But you will not always have me.'"; Mark gives what Matthew does not: the indignation was "to themselves" first, then spoken as a scolding.; Jesus' answer puts doing good to the poor in the hearers' own will ("whenever you want"). The poor are; named in the scolding. Jesus answers it, and the verses do not say what lay behind it in Mark. John; 12:6 says it of Judas, but John 12 is not in this set.

18114.text: Jealousy for another (1Ki 19:10, 14; Num 11:29).: Elijah says the same words twice, word for word: *"I have been very jealous for the Lord, the God of hosts … and I, even I only, am left, and they seek my life, to take it away"*. The first time is in the cave (19:10). The second is after the wind, the earthquake, the fire and "the sound of a low whisper" (19:12–14).; The encounter did not change how he described himself.; God does not argue with him. He gives him work: *"Go, return on your way … you shall anoint"* (19:15–16).; His zeal is joined in the same sentence to being alone and to his life being hunted. I read zeal for God that has turned into the sense of standing alone. God answers it with work, not with a correction.; Joshua's is also jealousy for another: *"Are you jealous for my sake? Would that all the Lord's people were prophets, that the Lord would put his Spirit on them!"* (Num 11:29). It is refused by the very person it is for.

18389.text: The risen Christ's own body. "See my hands and my feet, that it is I myself. Touch me, and see. For a spirit does not have flesh and bones as you see that I have" — said because "they … thought they saw a spirit". He ate fish before them; the apostles "ate and drank with him after he rose". Thomas: "put out your hand, and place it in my side". Yet he also came and "stood among them" with "the doors being locked", "vanished from their sight", and was at first not recognised (Mary, the Emmaus pair, the disciples at the lake).

19034.text: What follows at once: He asks for the earrings of the spoil (8:24).; *"Gideon made an ephod of it … And all Israel whored after it there, and it became a snare to Gideon and to his family"* (8:27).

19290.text: Luk 9:45–47: perception blocked from outside → fear to ask → rivalry → Jesus knows the reasoning of their hearts (v3)

19367.text: Candidate for the synthesis theme "the inner seat as governed" (v1 §R-V): v3 adds the interpreter's seat (Dan 5:12) and the diagnoser's reading of another's heart (Luk 9:47). Both are forms of "the seat of the other party". This is noted, not proposed.

19763.text: Mat 12:18 | soul (God's), Spirit | "with whom my soul is well pleased. I will put my Spirit upon him"

19781.text: Face: Chosen by God, rejected or hated by men (v2); Who: God, Jesus; Circumstance in the verses: "rejected by men but in the sight of God chosen"; "I chose you out of the world, therefore the world hates you"; scoffed "his Chosen One"; Verses: 1Pe 2:4, Joh 15:19, Luk 23:35

20565.text: *dialogizomai / dialogismos* | Honest troubled reasoning · hardened anxious reasoning · inner questioning seen by Jesus · reasoning together into murder · self-talk of the rich man · quarrel, dispute, opinions · argument about greatness · futile thinking · evil thoughts from the heart · partiality: "judges with evil thoughts" · thoughts revealed by the child set for a sign | Luk 1:29 · Mar 8:16–17; Mat 16:7–8 · Mar 2:6, 8; Luk 5:21–22; 6:8; 9:47 · Luk 20:14; Mat 21:25 · Luk 12:17 · 1Ti 2:8 ("without anger or quarreling"); Phili 2:14; Rom 14:1 · Luk 9:46 · Rom 1:21; 1Co 3:20 · Mar 7:21; Mat 15:19 · Jam 2:4 · Luk 2:35 | Inner reasoning becomes outward quarrel when it is shared and set on one's own standing (Luk 9:46; Rom 14:1) (R). The heart state decides honest or hardened (Luk 1:29 against Mar 8:17, S). In 1Ti 2:8 the quarrel word stands beside anger, a link to the anger strand

21281.text: Quiet here is only the state of a land, a realm, a sea, a place or a weapon (peace after war, calm water); it names no inner-being operation.

21283.text: Quiet is the inner calm and stillness of a person or God: a chosen or given settledness, or its refusal, that the verse commands, praises, laments the lack of, or promises.

21376.text: Fresh here describes a thing, a time or a figure (a new garment, a new cart, fresh water, an old pool, a parable of wineskins); no inner-being operation is voiced by it.

21391.text: Old here describes a thing, a time or a figure (a new garment, a new cart, fresh water, an old pool, a parable of wineskins); no inner-being operation is voiced by it.

21426.text: Rage here is the raging of the sea, a wind, a sword, a chariot, a beast or a vine in a figure of nature or war; no inner-being operation is voiced by it.

21520.text: Chooses is here God's (or Christ's) own choosing of persons or a people (the Lord chose Israel, a chosen race, the apostles whom he chose, my chosen); it is his outward act upon them and bears on their standing and response, named by other words of the verse.
